findings.title: Google Calendar refresh stores the safeParse wrapper as the credential key
findings.description: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data. The old code was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`, which returned the data. Line 97 assigns the wrapper to `key` and line 100 writes it to `credential.key`. The next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 then throws because `scope`, `access_token` and the rest are nested under `data`. This happens with the feature flag off, so every Google Calendar credential is corrupted on its first token refresh. Fix: persist `.data`.

findings.title: Salesforce service uses `prisma` without importing it
findings.description: The file never imports `@calcom/prisma` (imports are lines 1-20), yet line 96 calls `prisma.credential.update`. It type-checks only because `packages/prisma/index.ts:6-9` declares a global `var prisma`. That global is assigned only when `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`packages/prisma/index.ts:58-60`), so in production this is a `ReferenceError` and `getClient` rejects for every Salesforce credential. Fix: `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`.

findings.title: Salesforce `getClient` refreshes on every construction and discards the new token
findings.description:
Several problems in the new block:
- **Stale token:** the refreshed token is written to the DB, but `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` (lines 105-106). The refresh has no effect on the connection.
- **Unconditional refresh:** `getClient` runs from the constructor, so every instantiation makes a token request and a DB write with no expiry check.
- **Fragile status check:** line 86 uses `response.statusText !== "OK"`. `statusText` is empty over HTTP/2, which would make every refresh throw a 400; use `response.ok`.
- **Bypasses the new abstraction:** this is the only integration that calls `fetch` directly instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it ignores the sync endpoint while still using the sync-mode parser.
- **Dead branch:** lines 92-94 can never run, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure.

findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not validate what its comments claim
findings.description:
`[z.string().toString()]` is not a zod index signature. Zod schemas have no custom `toString`, so both computed keys evaluate to the literal `"[object Object]"` and the second overwrites the first. The effective schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys, sync mode drops the expiry and every other field. Consequences I traced:
- **Zoom:** `newTokens.expires_in` is undefined, so `expiry_date` becomes `NaN` (`zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:122`). That serialises to `null`, and the next `zoomTokenSchema.parse` fails.
- **Office365 calendar:** `expires_in` is never updated, so the token looks expired and is refreshed on every call.

Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` plus an explicit expiry field, or `z.record`.

findings.title: Placeholder `"refresh_token"` string can overwrite a real refresh token
findings.description:
When the parsed data has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string `"refresh_token"`, in both sync and non-sync mode. Callers then persist it:
- **Office365 calendar:** `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema` (line 56). If Microsoft omits it, line 264 spreads the placeholder over the stored token and line 270 saves it. The old code kept the existing token.
- **Zoom (sync mode):** `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` at `VideoApiAdapter.ts:120` stores the placeholder.

The helper also mutates the zod result in place and takes `response: any`. Callers should merge with the existing refresh token rather than receive a sentinel.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id where a user id is expected
findings.description: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credential.id`; the third parameter is `userId` and is sent as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. In sync mode this requests tokens for whichever user's id happens to equal the credential id, which can return another user's tokens. Every other call site passes `credential.userId`; `refreshAccessToken` here needs the user id threaded through from `biginAuth`.

findings.title: Sync-mode response shape is incompatible with most call sites
findings.description:
In sync mode the helper returns a raw `fetch` `Response`; otherwise it returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns. The `() => any` signature hides the mismatch. Callers that do not expect a `Response`:
- **Google** (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95`): `res?.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws; the catch swallows it and returns stale auth.
- **HubSpot** (`hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-198`): treats the `Response` as a `HubspotToken`, computes a `NaN` expiry and persists the `Response` object as the key.
- **Zoho CRM** (`zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217`) and **Zoho Bigin** (`zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96`): `tokenInfo.data.error` throws because `data` is undefined.

Only the fetch-based callers (Lark, Office365, Webex, Zoom) get a compatible type. The helper should be generic over the return type and normalise the sync response, with an `ok` check.

findings.title: Webhook resolves app metadata by slug, but the map is keyed by directory name
findings.description: `appStoreMetadata` is built from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`, whose keys are directory names (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`; lines 98-146). The handler indexes it with the DB slug, and the `as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata` cast hides the mismatch. Slugs that differ from their directory (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `zoom`, `msteams`) pass the `prisma.app` check and then return 404 at line 53. The endpoint only works for apps whose slug equals the directory name, such as `hubspot`, `salesforce`, `zohocrm`, `zoho-bigin` and `webex`. Look up by `Object.values(appStoreMetadata).find((m) => m.slug === app.slug)` or by the app's `dirName`.

findings.title: Webhook endpoint: weak secret comparison and unhandled failures
findings.description:
- **Secret comparison:** lines 24-27 use `!==`, which is not constant-time, on an endpoint that writes OAuth credentials for any user. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
- **No method restriction:** any HTTP verb is accepted.
- **Unhandled throws:** `schema.parse` (line 31), `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` (lines 57-59) all surface as 500s rather than 400s. The repo's `defaultHandler`/`defaultResponder` pattern, used in `larkcalendar/api/add.ts`, handles this.
- **No shape validation:** decrypted `keys` are written straight to `credential.key`.
- **Over-fetch:** `prisma.user.findUnique` at line 34 loads the full user row only to test existence.
- **Empty docblock:** `/** */` at line 16.

findings.title: Outbound sync request is unauthenticated and unchecked
findings.description: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. It sends no shared secret, although `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` exists for exactly this trust relationship, so the parent application cannot verify the caller before returning access tokens. There is also no `response.ok` check or error handling.

findings.title: `appSlug` passed for Zoom does not match the real slug
findings.description: The call passes `"zoomvideo"`, but the app's slug is `"zoom"` (`zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16`). Other call sites pass real slugs (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `msteams`). A sync endpoint keyed on Cal.com slugs, as the webhook is, will not recognise it. Hard-coded slug strings at eleven call sites invite this drift; derive them from each app's metadata or config.

findings.title: Office365 calendar loses diagnostics and keeps dead success checks
findings.description: The removed block logged the zod error and the Microsoft response on parse failure. Now the helper throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" with no detail. This is also a behaviour change: the old code continued and re-saved the existing credentials. The `tokenResponse.success &&` guard on line 264 is dead, as is the `!parsedToken.success` branch at `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:108-110`. Either return the data directly or keep safeParse semantics and let callers handle failure.

findings.title: No tests for the new credential-sync paths
findings.description: A repo-wide search found no test referencing `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens` or the `app-credential` webhook. A unit test of the parser alone would have caught the `[object Object]` schema, the placeholder token and the Google wrapper regression.

findings.title: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is a string, not a boolean
findings.description: The `&&` expression yields `string | undefined`, so the exported "ENABLED" constant holds the encryption key value when truthy. Wrap it in `Boolean(...)` or `!!` so the secret is not carried around under a flag name.

findings.title: Awkward relative imports and slug handling after the move
findings.description: The file now lives in `oauth/` but imports its sibling as `../oauth/decodeOAuthState`; `./decodeOAuthState` is the direct form. Separately, `zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` hard-codes `zoho-bigin` in the redirect URI while line 12 and `callback.ts` still use `appConfig.slug`.

findings.title: Import path updates for the moved OAuth helpers are complete
findings.description: A repo-wide search found no remaining imports of the old `_utils/createOAuthAppCredential`, `_utils/decodeOAuthState` or `_utils/encodeOAuthState` paths. The `../../types` and `../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` adjustments resolve to existing files. `credential` is in scope at the new `credential.userId` call sites in Lark, Office365 video, Webex, Zoom, HubSpot and Zoho CRM.
